title: fix: PIV functions only check SW 9000 on success — do not distinguish 6xxx error classes
description:
wp11_piv_sign, wp11_piv_generate_key, and wp11_piv_ecdh check only for SW 9000 success. Any non-9000 response returns the generic WP11_PIV_ERR_SW. Real tokens return many distinct 6xxx codes that need distinct handling:

- 6700: Wrong length (Lc or Le mismatch) — command construction bug, should never happen in production but if it does, CKR_FUNCTION_FAILED is wrong; should be CKR_ARGUMENTS_BAD or at least logged distinctly
- 6982: Security status not satisfied (PIN not verified, or PIN verification failed) — maps to CKR_USER_NOT_LOGGED_IN
- 6A80: Incorrect parameters in command data field — command construction bug
- 6A81: Function not supported by this token — maps to CKR_MECHANISM_INVALID or CKR_ACTION_PROHIBITED
- 6A88: Reference data not found (key slot empty) — maps to CKR_KEY_HANDLE_INVALID
- 6900: No precise diagnosis — log SW and return CKR_DEVICE_ERROR
- 6B00: Wrong P1/P2 — command construction bug, log it
- 6Dxx: Instruction not supported — applet confusion or wrong token type

Fix: Add a piv_sw_to_err(sw1, sw2) dispatch table in wp11_proto_piv.c that maps SW codes to typed wp11_piv_err_t values. Every PIV function's SW check becomes: return piv_sw_to_err(sw1, sw2); instead of bare WP11_PIV_ERR_SW. The PKCS#11 layer maps these to appropriate CKR_ codes.

Add a comment block at piv_sw_to_err listing the SP 800-73-4 and ISO 7816-4 sources for each mapping.
